textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 maths · Connecting the Dots... · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Suppose your teacher is meeting two childhood friends, one 5 feet tall and one 6 feet tall. You may guess that the first is a woman and the second a man.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Suppose your teacher is meeting two childhood friends, one 5 feet tall and one 6 feet tall. You may guess that the first is a woman and the second a man. You can be wrong, but men are more often taller than women.
beats.speakEn: Suppose your teacher is meeting two childhood friends, one 5 feet tall and one 6 feet tall. You may guess that the first is a woman and the second a man. You can be wrong, but men are more often taller than women.

beats.en: Comparing two batters is hard. One scored more in the first match, the other in the third. Totals are unfair when the number of matches differs. A representative value balances the highs and lows.
beats.speakEn: Comparing two batters is hard. One scored more in the first match, the other in the third. Totals are unfair when the number of matches differs. A representative value balances the highs and lows.

textbookBox.concept: Onion prices for twelve months at two towns can be compared in many ways: the highest price, the total, month-by-month comparison, or the difference between the highest and the lowest.
